differences.what: massing: the narrow brick front under its steep street hip, the long north flank running back past the round tower to the coped gables of the ranges and the garage, the two very tall stacks and the street dormers stand where the plate draws them, the stacks' tops, the tower's top and the hip's finial within about 10-30 px through this view's camera (fitted to them and the fence's foot)

the near stack's place: the plate stands it about 28 px (about 1.4 m) closer to the tower than the record does, as the 1919 programme plate's camera also finds (23 px) and the 1913 plate's does not; two of three plates against one, on stacks the cameras are fitted to, is a gap the fits disagree about

the third, smaller gable the plates draw at the flank's far end, coped and finialled as the ranges' are: T-3354 roofs the garage under a slated gable facing the flank, pitched 54 degrees to an apex at 15.7 m, with the ranges' stone coping, kneelers and 0.6 m finial (where it was flat in tin); through this camera its apex lands on the plate's third gable within about 15 px

the steep gables over the rear ranges, coped and finialled (T-3337), stand where the plate's two nearer gables do in kind and count; the small pinnacled dormers between the gables, on the rear range's slope facing the street: all three plates draw two, and T-3354 builds them (rear_wings.rear_range.roof.dormers, k01_wing_dormers): at v -3.85 and -2.3 m, their faces 0.3 m in from the range's wall line over the middle range's flat end, each a 1.0 m face with one tall light under a 60-degree stone-coped gable to its finial, a pinnacle at each edge; through this camera both land on the plate's two within about 10 px

the rear ranges' gables against all three Gatlin plates (T-3354): the MIDDLE range's gable now stands back 1.6 m from its north end over a flat deck (roof.flat_end) and is pitched 60 degrees, where it rose 50 degrees off the north wall; through the 1912, 1913 and 1919 cameras its finial now lands on the plates' highest gable within about 3 px across and 3 px up (it stood 25-30 px left and 30-60 px under). The rear range's gable apex, read again against all three Gatlin plates (T-3354, fifth run): the build's finial stands x 292 against about 327 on this coarser halftone (35 px) left of the plates' second gable, the same way in all three (the 1919 plate 26 px, the 1913 23 px, the 1912 about 35 px). It is not the plan: the middle range's finial and the plates' two dormers land within about 3-10 px, and no camera move closes it (walking the 1919 eye 10 m further back along its line of sight, focal re-scaled to hold the front, moves the apex 13 px further off). The one buildable reading that lands it is the rear range's north gable standing back about 1.45 m from its north wall over a flat deck, as the middle range's does: its apex then falls at x 445 on the 1919 plate (against 443), 273 on the 1913 (against 271) and 314 on the 1912 (against about 327). But the same plates draw the first of the two pinnacled dormers at v -3.85 m, within about 5-10 px of where it is built, which is 0.5 m in front of that set-back gable: a dormer cannot rise in front of the gable it stands behind, and set behind the gable's plane it lands 26, 23 and 20 px off in the three plates. So the plates' apex and their dormers disagree by about 1.3 m about where the rear range's gable stands, at the size of the cameras' own 25 px RMS residuals: within tolerance (T-3153), built as the 1911 trace and the dormers have it (L-k01-1919-range-dormers-3354)

the north flank's two-storey flat-topped bays and their mullioned windows: the plate draws the flank's lower storeys in deep shade behind the parkway trees; it confirms a flat-topped two-storey block under the far gables and pale corners at the ranges' steps, as the 1919 plate does, which T-3354 builds at the middle range's north-west corner (roof.flat_end); it resolves no window, no balustrade and none of the canted bay's own corners. T-3354 (third run) builds the two-light stone-mullioned window the 1913 and 1919 plates draw in each storey of the block's street face (rear_wings.mullioned), which this plate neither shows nor contradicts; the three-light groups those plates draw in its north face stay their open item

the street dormers: the broad three-light dormer and the small one-light dormer beside it, with the stack rising behind them at the front block's south side (T-3280, T-3301), stand over the plate's within about 30 px
the round tower's flat top under its heavy edge (T-3280), standing between the two tall stacks as the plate draws it
the front's lower storeys, the bow, the stoop and the entrance: the parkway trees and the hedge behind the fence hide them
the south neighbour (1923, the mansard at the plate's right edge), the parkway trees, the lamp post and the fence's pattern: not part of this record

_how: verdict is unreviewed | differs | matches, set by whoever compared the side-by-side with the picture; each difference is {what, status: open | fixed | not shown | within tolerance | owner ruling} — open only if a street visitor would notice it (over about 1 ft, missing, mis-shaped, miscounted, wrong material or colour), else within tolerance (T-3153); owner ruling where the owner asked the build to depart from the picture (T-3236).
